Detailed Description

Base class for a PSyIR node.

:param ast: reference into the fparser2 AST corresponding to this node.
:type ast: sub-class of :py:class:`fparser.two.Fortran2003.Base`
:param children: the PSyIR nodes that are children of this node.
:type children: list of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
:param parent: that parent of this node in the PSyIR tree.
:type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
:param annotations: Tags that provide additional information about \
    the node. The node should still be functionally correct when \
    ignoring these tags.
:type annotations: list of str

:raises TypeError: if a parent is supplied that is not an instance of Node.
:raises InternalError: if an invalid annotation tag is supplied.

360 def __init__(self, ast=None, children=None, parent=None, annotations=None):

362 raise TypeError(f"The parent of a Node must also be a Node but "
363 f"got '{type(parent).__name__}'")
364 self._disable_tree_update = True
365 # Keep a record of whether a parent node was supplied when constructing
366 # this object. In this case it still won't appear in the parent's
367 # children list. When both ends of the reference are connected this

394 def __eq__(self, other):
395 '''
396 Checks whether two nodes are equal. The basic implementation of this
397 checks whether the nodes are the same type, and whether all children
398 of the nodes are equal, and if so then
399 they are considered equal.
400
401 :param object other: the object to check equality to.
402
403 :returns: whether other is equal to self.
404 :rtype: bool
405 '''
406 super().__eq__(other)
407 is_eq = type(self) is type(other)
408 is_eq = is_eq and (len(self.children) == len(other.children))
409 for index, child in enumerate(self.children):
410 is_eq = is_eq and child == other.children[index]
411
412 return is_eq
413

1001 def _find_position(self, children, position=None):
1002 '''
1003 Recurse through the tree depth first returning position of
1004 a Node if found.
1005
1006 :param children: list of Nodes which are children of this Node.
1007 :type children: list of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
1008 :param int position: start counting from this position. Defaults to \
1009 START_POSITION.
1010
1011 :returns: if the self has been found in the provided children list \
1012 and its relative position.
1013 :rtype: bool, int
1014
1015 :raises InternalError: if the starting position is < 0.
1016
1017 '''
1018 if position is None:
1019 position = self.START_POSITION
1020 elif position < self.START_POSITION:
1021 raise InternalError(
1022 f"Search for Node position started from {position} "
1023 f"instead of {self.START_POSITION}.")
1024 for child in children:
1025 position += 1
1026 if child is self:
1027 return True, position
1028 if child.children:
1029 found, position = self._find_position(child.children, position)
1030 if found:
1031 return True, position
1032 return False, position
1033

1590 def _refine_copy(self, other):
1591 ''' Refine the object attributes when a shallow copy is not the most
1592 appropriate operation during a call to the copy() method.
1593
1594 :param other: object we are copying from.
1595 :type other: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.node.Node`
1596
1597 '''
1598 # Disable tree-updating during this operation (since it is a copy we
1599 # know we don't need to change the tree structure).
1600 self._disable_tree_update = True
1601 self._parent = None
1602 self._has_constructor_parent = False
1603 self._annotations = other.annotations[:]
1604 # Invalidate shallow copied children list
1605 self._children = ChildrenList(self, self._validate_child,
1606 self._children_valid_format)
1607 # And make a recursive copy of each child instead
1608 self.children.extend([child.copy() for child in other.children])
1609 self._disable_tree_update = False
1610

◆ _validate_child()

psyclone.psyir.nodes.node.Node._validate_child ( position,
child )
staticprotected 
 Decides whether a given child and position are valid for this node.
 The generic implementation always returns False, this simplifies the
 specializations as Leaf nodes will have by default the expected
 behaviour, and non-leaf nodes need to modify this method to its
 particular constraints anyway. Issue #765 explores if this method
 can be auto-generated using the _children_valid_format string.

:param int position: the position to be validated.
:param child: a child to be validated.
:type child: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`

980 def abs_position(self):
981 '''

Returns the closest preceding Node that this Node has a direct
dependence with or None if there is not one. Only Nodes with
the same parent as self are returned. Nodes inherit their
descendants' dependencies. The reason for this is that for
correctness a node must maintain its parent if it is
moved. For example a halo exchange and a kernel call may have
a dependence between them but it is the loop body containing
the kernel call that the halo exchange must not move beyond
i.e. the loop body inherits the dependencies of the routines

676 def backward_dependence(self):
677 '''Returns the closest preceding Node that this Node has a direct
678 dependence with or None if there is not one. Only Nodes with
679 the same parent as self are returned. Nodes inherit their
680 descendants' dependencies. The reason for this is that for
681 correctness a node must maintain its parent if it is
682 moved. For example a halo exchange and a kernel call may have
683 a dependence between them but it is the loop body containing
684 the kernel call that the halo exchange must not move beyond
685 i.e. the loop body inherits the dependencies of the routines
686 within it.'''
687 dependence = None
688 # look through all the backward dependencies of my arguments
689 for arg in self.args:
690 dependent_arg = arg.backward_dependence()
691 if dependent_arg:
692 # this argument has a backward dependence
693 node = dependent_arg.call
694 # if the remote node is deeper in the tree than me
695 # then find the ancestor that is at the same level of
696 # the tree as me.
697 while node.depth > self.depth:
698 node = node.parent
699 if self.sameParent(node) and node is not self:
700 # The remote node (or one of its ancestors) shares
701 # the same parent as me (but its not me)
702 if not dependence:
703 # this is the first dependence found so keep it
704 dependence = node
705 else:
706 # we have already found a dependence
707 if dependence.position < node.position:
708 # the new dependence is closer to me than
709 # the previous dependence so keep it
710 dependence = node
711 return dependence
712

532 def dag(self, file_name='dag', file_format='svg'):
533 '''
534 Create a dag of this node and its children, write it to file and
535 return the graph object.
536
537 :param str file_name: name of the file to create.
538 :param str file_format: format of the file to create. (Must be one
539 recognised by Graphviz.)
540
541 :returns: the graph object or None (if 'graphviz' is not found).
542 :rtype: :py:class:`graphviz.Digraph` or NoneType
543
544 :raises GenerationError: if the specified file format is not
545 recognised by Graphviz.
546
547 '''
548 try:
549 graph = graphviz.Digraph(format=file_format)
550 except ValueError as err:
551 raise GenerationError(f"unsupported graphviz file format "
552 f"'{file_format}' provided") from err
553 self.dag_gen(graph)
554 try:
555 graph.render(filename=file_name)
556 except graphviz.ExecutableNotFound as error:
557 print(error)
558 # TODO #11 add a warning to a log file here
559 # silently return if graphviz bindings are not installed
560 return None
561 return graph

563 def dag_gen(self, graph):
564 '''Output my node's graph (dag) information and call any
565 children. Nodes with children are represented as two vertices,
566 a start and an end. Forward dependencies are represented as
567 green edges, backward dependencies are represented as red
568 edges (but their direction is reversed so the layout looks
569 reasonable) and parent child dependencies are represented as
570 blue edges.'''
571 # Import outside top-level to avoid circular dependencies.
572 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches, import-outside-toplevel
573 from psyclone.psyir.nodes.loop import Loop
574 from psyclone.psyir.nodes.routine import Routine
575
576 # names to append to my default name to create start and end vertices
577 start_postfix = "_start"
578 end_postfix = "_end"
579 if self.children:
580 # I am represented by two vertices, a start and an end
581 graph.node(self.dag_name+start_postfix)
582 graph.node(self.dag_name+end_postfix)
583 else:
584 # I am represented by a single vertex
585 graph.node(self.dag_name)
586 # first deal with forward dependencies
587 remote_node = self.forward_dependence()
588 local_name = self.dag_name
589 if self.children:
590 # edge will come from my end vertex as I am a forward dependence
591 local_name += end_postfix
592 if remote_node:
593 # this node has a forward dependence
594 remote_name = remote_node.dag_name
595 if remote_node.children:
596 # the remote node has children so I will connect to
597 # its start vertex
598 remote_name += start_postfix
599 # Create the forward dependence edge in green
600 graph.edge(local_name, remote_name, color="green")
601 elif not isinstance(self, Routine):
602 # If this node is not a Routine (where the DAG context finishes)
603 # and has no forward dependence, connect it to the end vertex
604 # of its parent. Use blue to indicate a parent child
605 # relationship.
606 remote_name = self.parent.dag_name + end_postfix
607 graph.edge(local_name, remote_name, color="blue")
608 # now deal with backward dependencies. When creating the edges
609 # we reverse the direction of the dependence (place
610 # remote_node before local_node) to help with the graph
611 # layout
612 remote_node = self.backward_dependence()
613 local_name = self.dag_name
614 if self.children:
615 # the edge will come from my start vertex as I am a
616 # backward dependence
617 local_name += start_postfix
618 if remote_node:
619 # this node has a backward dependence.
620 remote_name = remote_node.dag_name
621 if remote_node.children:
622 # the remote node has children so I will connect to
623 # its end vertex
624 remote_name += end_postfix
625 # Create the backward dependence edge in red.
626 graph.edge(remote_name, local_name, color="red")
627 elif not isinstance(self, Routine):
628 # If this node is not a Routine (where the DAG context finishes)
629 # and has no backward dependence, connect it to the start vertex
630 # of its parent. Use blue to indicate a parent child
631 # relationship.
632 remote_name = self.parent.dag_name + start_postfix
633 graph.edge(remote_name, local_name, color="blue")
634 # now call any children so they can add their information to
635 # the graph
636 if isinstance(self, Loop):
637 # In case of a loop only look at the body (the other part
638 # of the tree contain start, stop, step values):
639 self.loop_body.dag_gen(graph)
640 else:
641 for child in self.children:
642 child.dag_gen(graph)
643

1285 def following(self, same_routine_scope=True, include_children=True):
1286 ''' Return all nodes after itself. Ordering is depth first. If the
1287 `same_routine_scope` argument is set to `True` (default) then only
1288 nodes inside the same ancestor routine are returned.
1289 If `include_children` is set to `True` (default) children of itself
1290 are also returned, otherwise it starts at the next sibiling.
1291
1292 :param bool same_routine_scope: an optional (default `True`) argument
1293 that restricts the returned nodes to those belonging to the same
1294 ancestor routine.
1295 :param bool include_children: an optional (default `True`) argument
1296 that enables including own children, instead of starting from
1297 the next sibiling.
1298
1299 :returns: the list of nodes that follow this one.
1300 :rtype: List[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`]
1301
1302 '''
1303 root = self.root
1304 if same_routine_scope:
1305 # Import here to avoid circular dependencies
1306 # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
1307 from psyclone.psyir.nodes import Routine
1308 # If there is an ancestor Routine node then only return nodes
1309 # that are within it.
1310 routine_node = self.ancestor(Routine)
1311 if routine_node:
1312 root = routine_node
1313
1314 if include_children:
1315 starting_node = self
1316 else:
1317 starting_node = self.following_node(same_routine_scope)
1318 if starting_node is None:
1319 return []
1320
1321 all_nodes = root.walk(Node)
1322 position = None
1323 for index, node in enumerate(all_nodes):
1324 if node is starting_node:
1325 if include_children:
1326 position = index + 1 # Skip self
1327 else:
1328 position = index
1329 break
1330
1331 return all_nodes[position:]

◆ forward_dependence()

psyclone.psyir.nodes.node.Node.forward_dependence ( self) 
Returns the closest following Node that this Node has a direct
dependence with or None if there is not one. Only Nodes with
the same parent as self are returned. Nodes inherit their
descendants' dependencies. The reason for this is that for
correctness a node must maintain its parent if it is
moved. For example a halo exchange and a kernel call may have
a dependence between them but it is the loop body containing
the kernel call that the halo exchange must not move beyond
i.e. the loop body inherits the dependencies of the routines
within it.

713 def forward_dependence(self):
714 '''Returns the closest following Node that this Node has a direct
715 dependence with or None if there is not one. Only Nodes with
716 the same parent as self are returned. Nodes inherit their
717 descendants' dependencies. The reason for this is that for
718 correctness a node must maintain its parent if it is
719 moved. For example a halo exchange and a kernel call may have
720 a dependence between them but it is the loop body containing
721 the kernel call that the halo exchange must not move beyond
722 i.e. the loop body inherits the dependencies of the routines
723 within it.'''
724 dependence = None
725 # look through all the forward dependencies of my arguments
726 for arg in self.args:
727 dependent_arg = arg.forward_dependence()
728 if dependent_arg:
729 # this argument has a forward dependence
730 node = dependent_arg.call
731 # if the remote node is deeper in the tree than me
732 # then find the ancestor that is at the same level of
733 # the tree as me.
734 while node.depth > self.depth:
735 node = node.parent
736 if self.sameParent(node) and node is not self:
737 # The remote node (or one of its ancestors) shares
738 # the same parent as me (but its not me)
739 if not dependence:
740 # this is the first dependence found so keep it
741 dependence = node
742 else:
743 if dependence.position > node.position:
744 # the new dependence is closer to me than
745 # the previous dependence so keep it
746 dependence = node
747 return dependence
748

1102 def get_sibling_lists(self, my_type, stop_type=None):
1103 '''
1104 Recurse through the PSyIR tree and return lists of Nodes that are
1105 instances of 'my_type' and are immediate siblings. Here 'my_type' is
1106 either a single class or a tuple of classes. In the latter case all
1107 nodes are returned that are instances of any classes in the tuple. The
1108 recursion into the tree is stopped if an instance of 'stop_type' (which
1109 is either a single class or a tuple of classes) is found.
1110
1111 :param my_type: the class(es) for which the instances are collected.
1112 :type my_type: type | Tuple[type, ...]
1113 :param stop_type: class(es) at which recursion is halted (optional).
1114 :type stop_type: Optional[type | Tuple[type, ...]]
1115
1116 :returns: list of lists, each of which containing nodes that are
1117 instances of my_type and are immediate siblings, starting at
1118 and including this node.
1119 :rtype: List[List[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`]]
1120
1121 '''
1122 # Separate nodes by depth
1123 by_depth = {}
1124 for node in self.walk(my_type, stop_type=stop_type):
1125 depth = node.depth
1126 if depth not in by_depth:
1127 by_depth[depth] = []
1128 by_depth[depth].append(node)
1129
1130 # Determine lists of consecutive nodes
1131 global_list = []
1132 for depth, local_list in sorted(by_depth.items()):
1133 block = []
1134 for node in local_list:
1135 if not block or node.immediately_follows(block[-1]):
1136 block.append(node)
1137 else:
1138 # Current node does not immediately follow the previous one
1139 # so this marks the end of the current block.
1140 global_list.append(block)
1141 block = [node]
1142 if block:
1143 global_list.append(block)
1144 return global_list

1466 def lower_to_language_level(self):
1467 '''
1468 In-place replacement of high-level concepts into generic language
1469 PSyIR constructs. This generic implementation only recurses down
1470 to its children, but this method must be re-implemented by Nodes
1471 that represent high-level concepts.
1472
1473 :returns: the lowered version of this node.
1474 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.node.Node`
1475
1476 '''
1477 # We recurse only over the original children (hence [:]), this is
1478 # because new nodes may be inserted during the lowering, but these
1479 # must already be language-level.
1480 for child in self.children[:]:
1481 child.lower_to_language_level()
1482 return self

1657 def origin_string(self):
1658 ''' Generates a string with the available information about where
1659 this node has been created. It currently only works with Fortran
1660 Statements or subchildren of them.
1661
1662 :returns: a string specifing the origin of this node.
1663 :rtype: str
1664 '''
1665 name = self.coloured_name(False)
1666 line_span = "<unknown>"
1667 original_src = "<unknown>"
1668 filename = "<unknown>"
1669 # Try to populate the line/src/filename using the ancestor Statement
1670 from psyclone.psyir.nodes.statement import Statement
1671 node = self.ancestor(Statement, include_self=True)
1672 # TODO #2062: The part below is tighly coupled to fparser tree
1673 # structure and ideally should be moved the appropriate frontend,
1674 # but we don't necessarely want to do all this string manipulation
1675 # ahead of time as it is rarely needed. One option is for the frontend
1676 # to provide a callable that this method will invoke to generate the
1677 # string. Other frontends or PSyIR not comming from code could provide
1678 # a completely different implementation in the Callable oject.
1679 if node and node._ast:
1680 if hasattr(node._ast, 'item') and node._ast.item:
1681 if hasattr(node._ast.item, 'reader'):
1682 if hasattr(node._ast.item.reader, 'file'):
1683 filename = node._ast.item.reader.file.name
1684 line_span = node._ast.item.span
1685 original_src = node._ast.item.line
1686 return (f"{name} from line {line_span} of file "
1687 f"'{filename}':\n> {original_src}")

1723 def path_from(self, ancestor):
1724 ''' Find the path in the psyir tree between ancestor and node and
1725 returns a list containing the path.
1726
1727 The result of this method can be used to find the node from its
1728 ancestor for example by:
1729
1730 >>> index_list = node.path_from(ancestor)
1731 >>> cursor = ancestor
1732 >>> for index in index_list:
1733 >>> cursor = cursor.children[index]
1734 >>> assert cursor is node
1735
1736 :param ancestor: an ancestor node of self to find the path from.
1737 :type ancestor: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
1738
1739 :raises ValueError: if ancestor is not an ancestor of self.
1740
1741 :returns: a list of child indices representing the path between
1742 ancestor and self.
1743 :rtype: List[int]
1744 '''
1745 result_list = []
1746 current_node = self
1747 while current_node is not ancestor and current_node.parent is not None:
1748 result_list.append(current_node.position)
1749 current_node = current_node.parent
1750
1751 if current_node is not ancestor:
1752 raise ValueError(f"Attempted to find path_from a non-ancestor "
1753 f"'{type(ancestor).__name__}' node.")
1754
1755 result_list.reverse()
1756 return result_list

1333 def preceding(self, reverse=False, same_routine_scope=True):
1334 ''' Return all nodes before itself. Ordering is depth first. If the
1335 `same_routine_scope` argument is set to `True` (default) then only
1336 nodes inside the same ancestor routine are returned. If the `reverse`
1337 argument is set to `True` then the node ordering is reversed i.e.
1338 returning the nodes closest to this node first.
1339
1340 :param bool reverse: an optional (default `False`) argument that
1341 reverses the order of any returned nodes (i.e. makes them 'closest
1342 first').
1343 :param bool same_routine_scope: an optional (default `True`) argument
1344 that restricts the returned nodes to those belonging to the same
1345 ancestor routine.
1346
1347 :returns: the nodes preceding this one in the PSyIR tree.
1348 :rtype: List[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`]
1349 '''
1350 root = self.root
1351 if same_routine_scope:
1352 # Import here to avoid circular dependencies
1353 # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
1354 from psyclone.psyir.nodes import Routine
1355 # If there is an ancestor Routine node then only return nodes
1356 # that are within it.
1357 routine_node = self.ancestor(Routine)
1358 if routine_node:
1359 root = routine_node
1360 all_nodes = root.walk(Node)
1361 position = None
1362 for index, node in enumerate(all_nodes):
1363 if node is self:
1364 position = index
1365 break
1366 nodes = all_nodes[:position]
1367 if reverse:
1368 nodes.reverse()
1369 return nodes

1689 def update_signal(self):
1690 '''
1691 Called whenever there is a change in the PSyIR tree below this node.
1692 It is responsible for ensuring that this method does not get called
1693 recursively and then calls the _update_node() method of the current

1701 return

840 def view(self, depth=0, colour=True, indent=" ", _index=None):
841 '''Output a human readable description of the current node and all of
842 its descendents as a string.
843
844 :param int depth: depth of the tree hierarchy for output \
845 text. Defaults to 0.
846 :param bool colour: whether to include colour coding in the \
847 output. Defaults to True.
848 :param str indent: the indent to apply as the depth \
849 increases. Defaults to 4 spaces.
850 :param int _index: the position of this node wrt its siblings \
851 or None. Defaults to None.
852
853 :returns: a representation of this node and its descendents.
854 :rtype: str
855
856 :raises TypeError: if one of the arguments is the wrong type.
857 :raises ValueError: if the depth argument is negative.
858
859 '''
860 # Avoid circular import
861 # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
862 from psyclone.psyir.nodes import Schedule
863
864 if not isinstance(depth, int):
865 raise TypeError(
866 f"depth argument should be an int but found "
867 f"{type(depth).__name__}.")
868 if depth < 0:
869 raise ValueError(
870 f"depth argument should be a positive integer but "
871 f"found {depth}.")
872 if not isinstance(colour, bool):
873 raise TypeError(
874 f"colour argument should be a bool but found "
875 f"{type(colour).__name__}.")
876 if not isinstance(indent, str):
877 raise TypeError(
878 f"indent argument should be a str but found "
879 f"{type(indent).__name__}.")
880
881 full_indent = depth*indent
882 description = self.node_str(colour=colour)
883 if not isinstance(self.parent, Schedule) or _index is None:
884 result = f"{full_indent}{description}\n"
885 else:
886 result = f"{full_indent}{_index}: {description}\n"
887 children_result_list = []
888 for idx, node in enumerate(self._children):
889 children_result_list.append(
890 node.view(
891 depth=depth + 1, _index=idx, colour=colour, indent=indent))
892 result = result + "".join(children_result_list)
893 return result
